outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
(a) Interval $KL$ or interval $LK$. Both names give the same two endpoints.
(b) Ray $KL$. It starts at $K$ and passes through $L$. Ray $LK$ starts at $L$ and goes through $K$, so it is different.
(c) Line $KL$ or line $LK$. Both names give the same line, which continues in both directions.

(a) The vertex is $N$. The arms are rays $NL$ (or $NM$) and $NP$.
(b) Keep the vertex in the middle. Choose one point on each arm.
$\angle LNP$, $\angle PNL$, $\angle MNP$ and $\angle PNM$.
(c) $\angle NLP$ puts $L$ in the middle, but the vertex is $N$.

The matching ticks show $PS=SQ$.
The matching single arcs show $\angle PRS=\angle SRQ$.

(a) Ray $DF$. Both rays start at $D$ and continue in the same direction through $E$ and $F$.

(b) Interval $DE$ ends at $E$, while interval $DF$ ends at $F$. Since $E$ lies between $D$ and $F$, interval $DF$ is longer.
